name: Lantana Boutique Hoi An Hotel
vi: Khách sạn Lantana Boutique Hội An
addr: 9 Thoại Ngọc Hầu, Minh An, Hội An
tip: North bank, ~350 m west of the Japanese Bridge. Outside the vehicle-free core, so a Grab can pull up to the door at any hour.
why: Base hotel
near: self

name: Bebe Tailor (Bebe 1)
hours: Daily, sources split between 08:00-20:00 and 08:00-21:30; Thursday is a normal trading day
tip: Three branches: Bebe 1 (05-07 Hoàng Diệu), Bebe 2 (95 Phan Châu Trinh), Bebe 3 (40 Trần Hưng Đạo). Bebe 1 is the main house with in-house tailors, so it is the one to use for a rush job.
why: Tailor option 1
near: East end of Ancient Town, ~1.2 km from Lantana

name: Yaly Couture Exclusive
addr: 47 Trần Phú, Minh An, Hội An
tip: Flagship in the Ancient Town core. Yaly's own guidance is a 3-day minimum for a suit; simple linen and cotton pieces are the ones they will turn round overnight.
why: Tailor option 2
near: Trần Phú, 2 min from Faifo Coffee

name: Yaly Couture Signature
hours: Daily, approx 08:00-21:30 (same group hours as Exclusive)
tip: Sits on the Nguyễn Thái Học artisan-shop street, so it drops into the Fri 09:00-11:30 block with no detour.
why: Tailor option 2b, on the planned shopping street
near: Nguyễn Thái Học artisan shops

name: Japanese Covered Bridge
addr: Trần Phú / Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Hội An
hours: Exterior open 24h; shrine interior with the Ancient Town ticket, approx 07:00-21:00
price: Covered by the 120,000 VND Ancient Town ticket (one tear-off stub)
tip: The 2022-2024 restoration is finished - it reopened in August 2024 and is fully open and scaffolding-free in 2026. Walking across is free; the stub is only taken to enter the shrine. Shoot it 06:30-07:30 for an empty frame.
why: Listed stop and the main photo spot
near: 350 m east of Lantana

name: Tan Ky Old House
price: One stub of the 120,000 VND Ancient Town ticket
tip: Ticketed site that shuts late afternoon, so keep it in the Fri 09:00-11:30 block rather than pushing it later.
why: Listed stop
near: Nguyễn Thái Học, opposite Morning Glory

name: Assembly Hall of the Fujian Chinese Congregation
price: One stub of the 120,000 VND Ancient Town ticket
tip: The most photogenic assembly hall (pink triple gate, hanging coil incense). Shoulders and knees covered.
why: Listed stop - assembly halls
near: Trần Phú, 3 min from Yaly Exclusive

name: Hoi An Ancient Town ticket booth
vi: Quầy vé phố cổ Hội An
addr: 11 booths ring the old town; nearest to Lantana is the one just behind the Japanese Bridge, others at the An Hội bridge foot and on Hai Bà Trưng
price: 120,000 VND foreigners, 80,000 VND Vietnamese; 5 tear-off stubs covering 5 of the 22 heritage sites
tip: Cannot be bought online - anything sold online is a reseller markup. Enforcement for simply walking the streets is loose; you need it for Tấn Ký, the assembly halls and the bridge interior.
why: Required for the ticketed sites on Friday morning
near: Japanese Bridge / An Hội Bridge

name: Rosie's Cafe
addr: 8/6 Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Hội An
tip: North bank, in the lane just past the Japanese Bridge - about 4 min on foot from Lantana and the closer of the two cafe options to the hotel.
why: Listed 11:45-12:45 cafe option
near: Japanese Bridge / Lantana

name: Cocobox
addr: 94 Lê Lợi, Minh An, Hội An
tip: Farm-to-table juice and deli bar inside the core, 3 min from Nước Mót - the 11:45-12:45 block works as one short loop.
why: Listed 11:45-12:45 cafe option
near: Lê Lợi, Ancient Town core

name: Nuoc Mot Hoi An
price: Approx 30,000-40,000 VND for the signature herbal iced tea
tip: The yellow wall is the photo itself - order the Mót herbal tea and shoot against it. Short queue before noon, long after 16:00.
why: Listed drink stop
near: Trần Phú, 100 m from Faifo Coffee

name: Madam Khanh - The Banh Mi Queen
addr: 115 Trần Cao Vân, Minh An, Hội An
tip: North of the old town, almost never a queue - the better of the two for a sit-down at 13:00. Cash.
why: Listed 13:00-14:00 option
near: Trần Cao Vân, 5 min north of the Ancient Town

name: Banh Mi Phuong
tip: The Bourdain one, so budget 15-30 min queuing at 13:00. It is 250 m from Bebe Tailor 1 - pair the two on one trip east.
why: Listed 13:00-14:00 option
near: Phan Châu Trinh, next to Bebe Tailor 1

name: Faifo Coffee
tip: The rooftop is the Xiaohongshu shot, looking down the tiled roofs of Trần Phú. Three floors - go straight to the top; the terrace is small and fills from about 15:30. Best light 16:30-17:30.
why: Listed 14:30-17:30 rooftop
near: Trần Phú, 100 m from Nước Mót

name: White Rose Restaurant
tip: The family workshop that supplies white-rose dumplings to most of the town, and you can watch them folded. It is ~900 m north-west of Trần Phú - a 10-12 min walk from Faifo, so treat it as its own leg, not a hop.
why: Listed 14:30-17:30 stop
near: Hai Bà Trưng, north of the Ancient Town

name: Hoai River lantern boat pier (Bach Dang / An Hoi bridge foot)
vi: Bến thuyền hoa đăng sông Hoài
addr: Bạch Đằng, at the An Hội footbridge, Hội An
price: Syndicate-fixed per BOAT: 150,000-170,000 VND for 1-3 people, 200,000-220,000 VND for 4-5. Floating lanterns 5,000-15,000 VND each, sold separately
tip: Buy at the official counter at the start of Bạch Đằng or at the An Hội bridge foot, not from touts on the promenade. The rate is per boat, not per head, so for two of you it is the 1-3 price. Ride is ~20 min between the An Hội and Cẩm Nam bridges. NOTE: Thu 24 Sep 2026 is the Full Moon Lantern Festival (lunar 14th) and Mid-Autumn eve, with the Ancient Town's electric lights off ~18:00-22:00 - that is the better boat night if they can reach the pier by ~21:45.
why: Listed 18:00-19:15 activity
near: Bạch Đằng riverfront

name: Bale Well
tip: Down a narrow alley off Trần Hưng Đạo. No menu - one fixed set per person (bánh xèo, nem lụi, spring rolls) and a staff member rolls the first one for you.
why: Listed 19:30-21:00 dinner option
near: Trần Hưng Đạo, north edge of the Ancient Town

name: Morning Glory Original
tip: Ms Vy's flagship and the busiest sit-down in the old town - book ahead for a 19:30 table. Directly opposite Tấn Ký Old House.
why: Listed 19:30-21:00 dinner option
near: Nguyễn Thái Học, opposite Tấn Ký

name: Hoi An Night Market (Nguyen Hoang street market)
addr: Nguyễn Hoàng, An Hội, Hội An
hours: Daily approx 17:00-23:00; many stalls start packing up around 21:00, food stalls run latest
tip: This is the realistic answer to the Thursday 21:30-23:00 snack window - it is the one place still cooking that late, and it is where bánh xoài and thịt xiên nướng are actually sold (they are street-cart food, not restaurant food). Lantern-lit street, so it doubles as the first photo stop. On Thu 24 Sep it is festival night, so the market and the whole An Hoi strip will be at maximum density.
why: Only reliably late-night food + the bánh xoài and thịt xiên nướng the plan asks for
near: Thu 21:30-23:00 late snacks; 550 m / 7 min walk from Lantana over the An Hội bridge

name: Trung Bac Restaurant (cao lau)
tip: A century-old shophouse doing the traditional version - closes in the evening, so it fits the Friday lunch window better than Thursday night.
why: The classic cao lầu house, 100+ years old, on the same block as the Friday walking route
near: Fri 09:00-11:30 Trần Phú block; 80 m from Hoi An Roastery, 100 m from Faifo Coffee

name: Quan Cao Lau Thanh
addr: 26 Thái Phiên, Minh An, Hội An
tip: Locals' choice, plastic-stool setting, no English menu needed - point at the one dish. Cash.
why: The cao lầu locals rate highest, and it is 130 m from Madam Khanh
near: Fri 13:00-14:00 Madam Khanh stop (2 min walk)

name: Quan Co Sau (mi Quang)
tip: Mì Quảng is a morning/lunch dish here - go before 12:00 or the broth is finished.
why: Closest proper mì Quảng to the hotel, on the north-bank walk back from Bale Well
near: Between Lantana and Bale Well on Trần Hưng Đạo, ~450 m from the hotel

name: Cong Caphe
addr: Công Nữ Ngọc Hoa, Hội An
tip: Opens early and does the coconut coffee; it is the nearest reliable sit-down breakfast/coffee to Lantana on the north bank, 300 m and no bridge crossing.
why: Breakfast spot near Lantana - useful on Sat morning before the 09:30 Grab
near: Lantana (4 min walk); also on the way to the Japanese Bridge

name: Cafe CitroNella
addr: 05 Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Hội An
tip: Sits on the quiet heritage lane immediately west of the Japanese Bridge - same old-house look as Trần Phú with a fraction of the crowd.
why: Second breakfast option, on the Lantana-to-Japanese-Bridge line
near: Japanese Covered Bridge (60 m) and Lantana (5 min)

name: Hoi An Roastery (Tran Phu)
tip: The Xiaohongshu shot here is the upstairs window with the paper-lantern light on the yellow wall - late afternoon sun comes through the lattice around 15:30-16:30. Several branches; the Trần Phú one is the photographed one.
why: Xiaohongshu-famous photo cafe, directly across from Faifo
near: Fri 14:30-17:30 Faifo Coffee block (60 m)

name: The Chef (rooftop)
tip: The backup if Faifo's small terrace is full - same tiled-roof view one block west, and usually seats available. Closer to the Japanese Bridge end.
why: Rooftop-view alternative to Faifo Coffee on the same street
near: Fri 14:30-17:30 Faifo Coffee block; 120 m from Nước Mót

name: Reaching Out Tea House
tip: Staffed by deaf artisans, so it is run in silence with wooden request blocks - the quietest room in the old town and zero effort. The attached shop sells their own ceramics and textiles, which is the best of the indie-boutique buys on Trần Phú.
why: Indie boutique shopping plus a genuinely restful stop between the tailor and the rooftop
near: Fri 09:00-11:30 Trần Phú artisan block; 40 m from Nước Mót

name: Banh Mi Ba Nga
tip: A cart, not a shop - the no-queue bánh mì inside the old town if Phượng's line is out the door at 13:00.
why: Third bánh mì, 20 m from Cocobox
near: Fri 11:45-12:45 Cocobox stop

name: An Hoi Bridge
addr: Bạch Đằng / Nguyễn Phúc Chu, Hội An
tip: Stand on the bridge facing east about 17:40-18:10 - the lanterns come on while there is still colour in the sky, which is the frame everyone posts. Then walk 100 m to the boat counter.
why: Sunset and lantern photo spot, immediately before the 18:00 boat
near: Fri 18:00 lantern boat pier (100 m); 500 m from Lantana

name: Cam Nam Bridge
addr: Bạch Đằng / Hoàng Diệu / Phan Bội Châu junction, Hội An
tip: Wider river and no crowd compared with the An Hội bridge; best 17:30-18:30. It is the far east end of the riverfront, so use it only if you shift dinner east toward Bebe/Bánh Mì Phượng.
why: The uncrowded sunset viewpoint over the Thu Bồn
near: East end of Bạch Đằng riverfront, 350 m from Bebe Tailor 1

name: Hoi An Full Moon Lantern Festival (Mid-Autumn eve)
vi: Lễ hội đèn lồng đêm rằm Hội An / Tết Trung Thu
addr: Ancient Town streets and the Hoài River waterfront, Hội An
hours: Thu 24 Sep 2026, electric street lighting off approx 18:00-22:00; lantern parades and lion dances through the evening
tip: Falls on the 14th of each lunar month; 2026 dates are 27 Jul, 26 Aug, 24 Sep, 23 Oct, 22 Nov, 22 Dec. The 24 Sep one is Mid-Autumn eve and one of the two biggest nights of the year. Their 21:30 arrival catches only the last ~30 min of the lights-off window - go straight out from the hotel without unpacking. Fri 25 Sep is Tet Trung Thu itself: not a public holiday, so shops trade normally, but restaurants fill - book Morning Glory.
why: Falls on their arrival night and changes the Thursday evening plan
near: Thu 24 Sep 21:30-23:00 walk; An Hoi bridge and Bach Dang riverfront
